properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 6 at 8:21PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

caused Moderate flooding at the gauge west of Cocoa. The river is
forecast to slowly rise into Major flood stage this weekend and into
early next week.

forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Friday the stage was 16.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Friday was 16.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 16.9 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 1130 AM EST.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued November 6 at 5:22PM MST until November 6 at 11:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 1115 PM MST.

* At 522 PM MST, National Weather Service Flagstaff Doppler radar
indicated heavy rainfall in the West Clear Creek drainage from
earlier thunderstorms. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Verde Lakes, Hanging Garden, Indian Maiden Falls and West Clear
Creek Wilderness.

This includes State Route 260 between mile markers 225 and 229.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Clear Creek Group Campgrounds.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Bull Pen Day Use Area, West Clear Creek near the campground and
Indian Maiden Falls.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Verde River near the confluence of West Clear Creek and West Clear
Creek.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued November 6 at 7:44PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Anegada Passage east of Virgin Gorda and Saint Croix south to 17N...
Coastal waters east of Puerto Rico, around Vieques, and around and
just north of Culebra and Saint John...
Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the
coastal waters of Saint Croix...

* At 744 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots and possible
waterspouts. These strong thunderstorms were located across the
Caribbean offshore waters and the Anegada Passage, approaching
coastal waters of St. Croix, moving north at 15 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Anegada Passage east of Virgin Gorda and
Saint Croix south to 17N, Coastal waters east of Puerto Rico,
around Vieques, and around and just north of Culebra and Saint John
and Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including
the coastal waters of Saint Croix.
properties.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, heavy downpours, and waterspouts. Boaters
should seek safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.
properties.area: Anegada Passage east of Virgin Gorda and Saint Croix south to 17N; Coastal Waters east of Puerto Rico, around Vieques, and around and just north of Culebra and Saint John; Caribbean Waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the Coastal Waters of Saint Croix
